{"response":"The proposed factorial bound is false: `16! = 20,922,789,888,000`, which is much larger than `80325`. The useful observation is that `17 ∣ 80325`, so `17 ∣ n!`; since 17 is prime, the factorial divisibility lemma gives `17 ≤ n`.

```lean
  have hp : Nat.Prime 17 := by norm_num
  have hd : 17 ∣ 80325 := by norm_num
  have hdiv : 17 ∣ n ! := dvd_trans hd h₁
  exact (hp.dvd_factorial h₀).mp hdiv
```

I have not checked the proof in Lean, so the precise arguments expected by `Nat.Prime.dvd_factorial` may need adjustment."}
